item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Aug 11, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Aug 13, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: The Doo Wop Project: Echos of the Street at American Music Theatre — Sat Aug 15 — American Music Theatre
item.description: The dynamic Broadway stars of The Doo Wop Project are on a mission to put Doo Wop on everyone’s playlist! With their smokin’ hot band, they capture and deliver the classic sounds of the guys who, back in the day, harmonized with each other on stoops, in the subway, and on street corners, and they have also created a unique, exciting, fun way to “Doowop-ify” today’s biggest hits – reimagining them as though they had been written during the Doo Wop era! Once you experience The Doo Wop Project live on stage, you’ll see why everyone around the country calls them AMERICA’S PREMIERE DOO WOP GROUP. Their brand new 90 minute show — “Echoes of the Street” — keeps the classic sounds of Doo Wop alive for audiences of all ages. You’ll hear Doo Wop classics like the Del Vikings’ “Whispering Bells”, The Tymes’ “So Much in Love”, The Marcels’ “Blue Moon”, The Four Seasons’ “Sherry” and Motown’s “My Girl”. And you’ll fall in love with The Doo Wop Project’s Doowop-ified versions of contemporary songs

item.title: 48th Annual Long's Park Art Festival — Fri Sep 4, 9:00 AM — Long’s Park
item.description:
What began as a local fundraiser in 1979 has evolved into one of the nation’s premier outdoor art events. Every Labor Day weekend, the Long’s Park Art Festival transforms the park into a vibrant, three-day gallery showcasing over 200 juried exhibitors from across the country. Attracting thousands of art lovers from across the Mid-Atlantic, the festival celebrates creative talent while directly funding Long’s Park’s beloved Summer Music Series.Tickets are available to purchase on the Long’s Park website or you can purchase them at the door. Guest ages 25 and under are free.

item.description:

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.description:
PDF@Zoetropolis presents Barry Jenkins’ Moonlight. The next film in our America 250 series—and the second in our three-film exploration of Reinvention and Transformation.
Told across three defining periods in one life, Moonlight follows Chiron as he grows up in Miami and struggles with the names others give him, the expectations of masculinity, and his longing to be known. Visually breathtaking and deeply humane, the film explores identity, race, sexuality, vulnerability, and the rare moments of tenderness that make another way of living possible. America celebrates the self-made individual—but who is truly free to reinvent themselves? And what happens when the identity we construct to survive becomes a form of armor?
